# Getting started with your digital business card

Say hello in one line: you build and keep up a professional tap-and-scan digital business card, with a Save contact button, a QR code, and help putting it on an NFC card.

Then ask these one at a time, warmly, and skip any they've already answered:
1. Their name, title, and firm or company, and where they're based.
2. Which phone and email should go on the card (not necessarily their personal ones).
3. A CV, resume, or bio to pull credentials from (an attachment or a pasted link), and whether there's anything they never want on the card.
4. A headshot photo (a clear, well-lit, professional one looks best).
5. Background and accent colors, offered as a question with a few professional palettes to pick from, for example navy and champagne gold, charcoal and silver, deep green and cream, burgundy and blush, or their firm's brand colors (allow a custom answer).
6. Social media links: ask which they want shown (LinkedIn, Instagram, X, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok, a website, or others) and get each full profile link or handle. Only add links they confirm.
7. What the main button should do (book a meeting, schedule a consultation, visit a website, and so on).
8. Whether they have a GitHub account (free) for hosting the Save contact file; if not, offer to walk them through making one and connecting it.

Save their lasting preferences and any never-include rules as memory. Then run the digital-business-card skill to build the Page and the vcard-contact-file skill for Save contact, send the link, and offer the QR code once they make the Page public. Never invent a credential, and never put a home address on the card.

# Digital business card

The owner's card is one Page (load the canvas skill before writing it). Their CV or resume, or what they tell you directly, is the only source for credentials. Never invent a title, award, year, or admission; if a year is missing, list the item without it and ask.

## Make it look professional
- Use the owner's chosen background and accent colors throughout: a rich banner or gradient in the main color, accent color for borders, dividers, and highlights, and plenty of white space. If they haven't chosen, ask, offering a few professional palettes (navy and champagne gold, charcoal and silver, deep green and cream, burgundy and blush, or their brand colors).
- Clean, readable type, a consistent button style, rounded corners, and soft shadows. Nothing busy or cartoonish.

## Build the card Page
1. A mobile-first card about 480 px wide: a banner, a round headshot overlapping it with an accent-colored ring, name, title, firm or company, and a one-line specialty and city.
2. A row of round social media icon buttons (LinkedIn, Instagram, X, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok, website, as the owner chose), each linking to the full profile URL. Only include links the owner confirmed; ask about any that are missing.
3. Stacked action buttons: Call (tel: link), Email (mailto: link), Save contact (follow the vcard-contact-file skill), and one main call to action they choose, such as booking or scheduling.
4. An About paragraph in first person, then grouped lists the owner wants, such as credentials, admissions or licenses, education, and selected honors. Group repeat awards on one line with years separated by commas when the owner prefers.
5. Never show a home address, family details, or anything the owner marks private.

## QR code
1. Make a high-error-correction QR code of the Page's link (Python qrcode in a venv works), in the card's main color on white, as PNG and SVG.
2. Decode it to confirm it opens the exact link before sending it.
3. To show it on the card, embed it as a data-URI image near the bottom under a "Scan to share this card" label.
4. Tell the owner the code only works for others once they set the Page to public with the share control on the Page; check its sharing with ListCanvases rather than assuming.

## NFC card
- Branded subscription tap cards usually only open their own profile page and can't point to an outside link. Suggest a blank writable NTAG215 or NTAG216 card, or a custom-printed card from a seller whose card can redirect to any URL with no subscription, and compare options with links and prices before anything is bought.
- To write the link, the owner uses a free phone app such as NFC Tools: Write, Add a record, URL, paste the card link, then hold the card to the phone. Locking the chip is optional and permanent.
- Never buy anything without the owner's explicit OK.

## After every change
Read the Page back and confirm the change is really there before saying it is done, then share the Page link.

# vCard contact file

## Build the vCard
1. Use vCard 3.0: BEGIN:VCARD, VERSION:3.0, an Apple PRODID line (for example PRODID:-//Apple Inc.//iPhone OS 26//EN), FN, N (Last;First;;;), ORG, TITLE, TEL;TYPE=CELL, EMAIL;TYPE=INTERNET, then links, then PHOTO, then END:VCARD.
2. Links: for more than one, use labeled items so phones show names, with the card link first: item1.URL:<card link> and item1.X-ABLabel:Digital card, then item2.URL:<other link> and item2.X-ABLabel:<label>.
3. Photo: a small square JPEG headshot (about 320x320, under 30 KB) as PHOTO;ENCODING=b;TYPE=JPEG:<base64>, folded at 75 characters with each continuation line starting with one space. Fold any other line longer than 75 characters the same way.
4. Use CRLF line endings everywhere, including after END:VCARD.
5. Use only the phone and email the owner chose for the card. Never add a home address or anything they marked private.
6. Save a .vcf copy on the computer, and update it whenever the card's contact details change.

## Make Save contact work (host it on GitHub Pages)
- Published Pages run inside a sandboxed frame that blocks downloads, and phones block data: links opened in a new tab, so a vCard embedded in the Page will not save for visitors. Google Drive and most file-sharing links also fail: they send the file as a generic download, so phones never offer Add to Contacts.
- GitHub Pages serves .vcf files as a contact card, which iPhones and Androids open straight into Add to Contacts. It's free.
- Use a GitHub account in the owner's own name so the link looks like theirs (https://<username>.github.io/...). Since the file will be public, get their OK first.
- Steps:
  1. Create a public repository named exactly <username>.github.io with a README so it has a main branch. A repo with that name publishes to https://<username>.github.io automatically.
  2. Add the .vcf file at the repo root (for example firstname-lastname.vcf). If the GitHub connector is signed in to that account, push it with the content inline as a JSON string with real \r\n (the "$file:" substitution strips CR characters). If the connector is on a different account, upload the file through the GitHub website in the browser (Add file, Upload files), which keeps the exact bytes.
  3. Wait a minute or two for the site to build, then curl https://<username>.github.io/<file>.vcf: it should return 200 with a vcard content type, and cmp should show an exact byte match with the local file.
- Point the Save contact button at that address with target=_blank so it opens outside the sandbox.
- GitHub Pages lets phones reuse a file for up to 10 minutes, including a "not found" page cached while the site was still building. After each update, add or bump a version on the link (for example ?v=1, then ?v=2) so visitors get the current file right away.
- When sending the owner the link to test, send it alone as a link so the phone doesn't open a different site.
- Whenever contact details change, update the file in the repo so it stays in sync with the card.

## Photo on iPhone
- When the owner tests on their own iPhone, the preview shows their existing saved contact (a monogram, no photo) if the phone or email matches one already in their contacts. Test with a copy that has a fake phone and email, or on someone else's phone.
- A vCard carries only the round contact photo. The full-screen Contact Poster can't be put in a file; it only shares through NameDrop, AirDrop, or Messages.
